- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment spikes) — model tends to overshoot after sentiment improves.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment — model underreacts to bearish signals, especially when sentiment is consistently negative.
- Lag in price response to sentiment shifts — model often delays price adjustments, especially when sentiment turns from negative to neutral or positive.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model overreacts to recent highs, leading to exaggerated upward forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias — model tends to overcorrect downward after sharp rises, especially when sentiment is mixed or neutral.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is negative — model fails to account for short-term volatility.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is >0.1 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
